'''Alexander "Alex" Lubotzky''' ({{langx|he|אלכסנדר לובוצקי}}; born 28 June 1956) is an Israeli mathematician and former politician. He is a professor of mathematics at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] and professor emeritus at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], where he held the Maurice and Clara Weil Chair in Mathematics.<ref name="weizmann">{{cite web |title=Prof. Alexander Lubotzky: Bridging the abstract and the applicable |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/WeizmannCompass/sections/new-scientists/prof-alexander-lubotzky |website=Weizmann Compass |publisher=[[Weizmann Institute of Science]] |date=16 November 2021 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref> He served as a member of the [[Knesset]] for [[Third Way (Israel)|The Third Way]] party from 1996 to 1999.<ref name="amacad">{{cite web |title=Alexander Lubotzky |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/alexander-lubotzky |publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref> Lubotzky is a leading researcher in [[group theory]] and its applications to [[combinatorics]] and [[theoretical computer science]], known in particular for the construction of [[Ramanujan graph]]s and for the theory of high-dimensional expanders. He received the [[Israel Prize]] in mathematics and computer science in 2018.<ref name="toi">{{cite news |title=Former MK awarded Israel Prize for math and computer science |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/former-mk-awarded-israel-prize-for-math-and-computer-science/ |work=[[The Times of Israel]] |agency=JTA |date=21 February 2018 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

== Biography ==
=== Early life and education ===
Lubotzky was born in [[Ramat Gan]] to parents who were [[Holocaust survivors]].<ref name="nonmathcv">{{cite web |title=Professor Alex Lubotzky (non-mathematical CV) |url=https://ma.huji.ac.il/~alexlub/CV/non-mathematical-cv.pdf |publisher=[[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="hayadan">{{cite news |title=Winner of the Israel Prize in Mathematics and Computer Science – Prof. Alex Lubotzky |url=https://hayadan.com/alex-lubotzky-israel-prime-mathematics-and-computer-science-2102182 |work=Hayadan |date=21 February 2018 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>{{efn|The Weizmann Institute profile gives his birthplace as [[Tel Aviv]] and states that he was raised in Ramat Gan.<ref name="weizmann" />}} His father, the lawyer [[Iser Lubotzky]], was a member of the [[Vilna Ghetto]] underground and a [[Jewish partisans|partisan]], an officer in the [[Irgun]], and later the legal adviser of the [[Herut]] movement; his mother, Rivka, survived the war as a girl in the forests of Poland and reached [[Mandatory Palestine]] via [[Cyprus internment camps|Cyprus]].<ref name="hayadan" /><ref>{{cite book |last=Lubotzky |first=Asael |author-link=Asael Lubotzky |title=Not My Last Journey |language=he |publisher=[[Yedioth Ahronoth|Yedioth Books]] |year=2017}}</ref>

While still in high school, Lubotzky began studying mathematics at [[Bar-Ilan University]], receiving his BSc ''summa cum laude'' in 1975.<ref name="weizmann" /> He continued directly to doctoral studies under [[Hillel Furstenberg]] within the [[Atuda|Israel Defense Forces academic reserve]] programme, and completed his PhD in 1979, at the age of 23, with a thesis on profinite groups and the [[congruence subgroup problem]].<ref name="cv">{{cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae – Alexander Lubotzky |url=http://www.ma.huji.ac.il/~alexlub/CV/CV_2026.pdf |publisher=Hebrew University of Jerusalem |year=2026 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=22528}}</ref> He served in the [[Israel Defense Forces]] from 1977 to 1982 as an officer in a research and development unit, and was discharged with the rank of captain.<ref name="nonmathcv" /><ref name="hayadan" />

=== Academic career ===
On completing his military service in 1982, Lubotzky joined the Einstein Institute of Mathematics of the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] as a senior lecturer. He was promoted to associate professor in 1985, at the age of 29, reportedly becoming the youngest professor in Israel at the time, and to full professor in 1989.<ref name="cv" /><ref name="hayadan" /> He later held the Maurice and Clara Weil Chair in Mathematics.<ref name="toi" /> He chaired the Einstein Institute of Mathematics from 1994 to 1996.<ref name="nonmathcv" />

Lubotzky was editor-in-chief of the ''[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]'' from 1990 to 1995 and remains on its editorial board; he has also served on the editorial boards of the ''[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]'', the ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'', the ''[[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]]'' and other journals, and chaired the general editorial board of [[Magnes Press]] from 2004 to 2011.<ref name="cv" /><ref name="hayadan" /> In 2005–2006 he led a year-long special programme at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton on Lie groups, representations and discrete mathematics.<ref name="jmm2011">{{cite web |title=2011 Joint Mathematics Meetings – Highlighted speakers: Alexander Lubotzky |url=https://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm-archive/2125_speakers.html |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Lubotzky |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/alexander-lubotzky |publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref> He was president of the [[Israel Mathematical Union]] in 2019–2020.<ref name="weizmann" />

He has held visiting positions at [[Princeton University]], [[Yale University]], [[Columbia University]], [[Stanford University]], the [[University of Chicago]], the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[ETH Zurich]], the [[Fields Institute]] and the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and in 2012 was a visiting researcher at [[Microsoft Research]] New England.<ref name="cv" /><ref name="weizmann" /> He was an adjunct professor at Yale from 1999.<ref name="cv" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics |url=https://catalog.yale.edu/ycps/subjects-of-instruction/mathematics/ |work=Yale College Programs of Study 2024–2025 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

Two conferences of the Midrasha Mathematicae series of the [[Israel Institute for Advanced Studies]] have been held in his honour: the 20th Midrasha in November 2016, marking his 60th birthday,<ref>{{cite web |title=The 20th Midrasha Mathematicae celebrating Alex Lubotzky's 60th Birthday |url=http://www.as.huji.ac.il/schools/math20 |publisher=[[Israel Institute for Advanced Studies]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191019142033/http://www.as.huji.ac.il:80/schools/math20 |archive-date=19 October 2019 |url-status=dead |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref> and the 25th Midrasha, "Groups, Expanders and Codes", in June 2026, marking his 70th.<ref>{{cite web |title=The 25th Midrasha Mathematicae on Groups, Expanders and Codes – Celebrating the 70's birthday of Alex Lubotzky |url=https://iias.huji.ac.il/event/25th-midrasha-mathematicae-groups-expanders-and-codes |publisher=Israel Institute for Advanced Studies |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

In 2021 Lubotzky joined the Department of Mathematics of the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] as a full professor.<ref name="weizmann" />

=== Political and public activity ===
Lubotzky was a founding member of [[Third Way (Israel)|The Third Way]] party in 1996 and was elected on its list to the 14th Knesset. He sat on the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, the Constitution, Law and Justice Committee, the Science and Technology Committee and the Committee on the Status of Women, and chaired the subcommittee on the [[Year 2000 problem]].<ref name="nonmathcv" /><ref name="amacad" /><ref name="knesset">{{cite web |title=Alexander Lubotzky |url=https://main.knesset.gov.il/en/MK/APPS/mk/mk-personal-details/71 |publisher=[[Knesset]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

In the Knesset he was known chiefly for his compromise proposals on religion-and-state issues. Together with [[Yossi Beilin]] and others he drafted the 1998 "Beilin–Lubotzky Covenant", a proposed social contract between religious and secular Israelis, and during the "[[Who is a Jew?]]" conversion-law crisis he played a mediating role and accompanied the work of the [[Yaakov Neeman|Ne'eman]] Committee on conversion.<ref name="nonmathcv" /><ref name="hayadan" /> He left politics at the end of the 14th Knesset in 1999 and returned to full-time academic work.<ref name="amacad" />

Lubotzky has also served on the board of the [[Beit Morasha]] study centre (1987–2005), the public board of governors of the [[National Library of Israel]] (2005–2012) and the public council of [[Yad Izhak Ben-Zvi]] (2011–2015).<ref name="cv" /> In 2002 he was appointed arbitrator in the dispute between the Hebrew University and [[Amnon Shashua]] over the intellectual property of [[Mobileye]]; the parties reached a settlement in 2004 on the basis of his proposal.<ref>{{cite news |title=התרגיל שעשה מייסד מובילאיי לאוניברסיטה העברית – ימים לפני עסקת המיליארדים עם אינטל |trans-title=The manoeuvre Mobileye's founder pulled on the Hebrew University – days before the billion-dollar deal with Intel |url=https://www.themarker.com/markets/2017-09-06/ty-article/0000017f-edaa-d4cd-af7f-edfaaacb0000 |work=[[TheMarker]] |language=he |date=6 September 2017 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==
Lubotzky's research centres on group theory in a broad sense: finite and infinite groups, topological, algebraic and arithmetic groups, and their connections with [[representation theory]], [[number theory]], geometry and combinatorics.<ref name="hayadan" /> The Israel Prize committee described him as "one of the most important researchers in the world in group theory" whose work "influenced many fields in mathematics and computer science, especially in the area of expander graphs and their applications".<ref name="toi" /> Among his main contributions:

* '''Ramanujan graphs and expanders.''' With [[Ralph S. Phillips|Ralph Phillips]] and [[Peter Sarnak]], Lubotzky constructed the first infinite families of [[Ramanujan graph]]s: [[regular graph]]s whose spectral gap is optimal, and hence [[expander graph]]s with the best possible spectral expansion. The construction combines representation theory with deep results from number theory, in particular the [[Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lubotzky |first1=Alexander |last2=Phillips |first2=Ralph |last3=Sarnak |first3=Peter |title=Ramanujan graphs |journal=[[Combinatorica]] |volume=8 |issue=3 |year=1988 |pages=261–277 |doi=10.1007/BF02126799}}</ref>
* '''High-dimensional expanders and Gromov's topological overlap problem.''' Lubotzky was among the founders of the theory of expanding [[simplicial complex]]es ("high-dimensional expanders"). With [[David Kazhdan]] and [[Tali Kaufman]] he gave a partial solution to [[Mikhael Gromov (mathematician)|Gromov]]'s topological overlap problem by constructing bounded-degree topological expanders from Ramanujan complexes;<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kaufman |first1=Tali |last2=Kazhdan |first2=David |last3=Lubotzky |first3=Alexander |title=Isoperimetric inequalities for Ramanujan complexes and topological expanders |journal=[[Geometric and Functional Analysis]] |volume=26 |year=2016 |pages=250–287 |doi=10.1007/s00039-016-0362-y}}</ref> the problem was subsequently solved in every dimension by his student [[Shai Evra]] together with Kaufman.<ref>{{cite conference |last1=Evra |first1=Shai |last2=Kaufman |first2=Tali |title=Bounded degree cosystolic expanders of every dimension |book-title=Proceedings of the 48th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC 2016) |year=2016 |pages=36–48 |doi=10.1145/2897518.2897543 |arxiv=1510.00839}}</ref>
* '''Good locally testable codes.''' With [[Irit Dinur]], Shai Evra, Ron Livne and [[Shahar Mozes]], Lubotzky gave the first explicit construction of [[locally testable code]]s with constant rate, constant relative distance and constant locality ("c³-LTCs"), settling a long-standing open problem in coding theory. The construction is based on a new two-dimensional object, the left-right Cayley complex.<ref name="ltc">{{cite conference |last1=Dinur |first1=Irit |last2=Evra |first2=Shai |last3=Livne |first3=Ron |last4=Lubotzky |first4=Alexander |last5=Mozes |first5=Shahar |title=Locally testable codes with constant rate, distance, and locality |book-title=Proceedings of the 54th Annual ACM SIGACT Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC 2022) |year=2022 |pages=357–374 |doi=10.1145/3519935.3520024 |arxiv=2111.04808}}</ref>
* '''Explicit lossless expanders.''' With Jun-Ting Hsieh, Sidhanth Mohanty, Assaf Reiner and Rachel Yun Zhang, he gave the first explicit construction of constant-degree two-sided lossless vertex expanders, resolving another long-standing open question; the graphs also yield new families of quantum [[Low-density parity-check code|LDPC]] codes with linear-time decoding.<ref name="lossless">{{cite arXiv |last1=Hsieh |first1=Jun-Ting |last2=Lubotzky |first2=Alexander |last3=Mohanty |first3=Sidhanth |last4=Reiner |first4=Assaf |last5=Zhang |first5=Rachel Yun |title=Explicit lossless vertex expanders |year=2025 |eprint=2504.15087 |class=math.CO}}</ref><ref name="focs25">{{cite web |title=Paper Awards – FOCS 2025 |url=https://focs.computer.org/2025/best-paper-awards/ |publisher=[[IEEE Computer Society]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* '''Profinite methods; conjectures of Serre and Malcev.''' Lubotzky developed the technique of studying a discrete group through its [[profinite group|profinite]] (or pro-''p'') completion, applying analytic and topological tools to the completion and drawing conclusions about the original group. In this way he proved [[Jean-Pierre Serre]]'s conjecture that the fundamental groups of finite-volume [[hyperbolic 3-manifold]]s do not have the [[congruence subgroup property]],<ref>{{cite journal |last=Lubotzky |first=Alexander |title=Free quotients and the congruence kernel of SL<sub>2</sub> |journal=[[Journal of Algebra]] |volume=77 |issue=2 |year=1982 |pages=411–418 |doi=10.1016/0021-8693(82)90263-0}}</ref> and gave a group-theoretic characterisation of finitely generated [[linear group]]s, answering questions posed by [[Anatoly Maltsev]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Lubotzky |first=Alexander |title=A group theoretic characterization of linear groups |journal=Journal of Algebra |volume=113 |issue=1 |year=1988 |pages=207–214 |doi=10.1016/0021-8693(88)90190-1}}</ref>
* '''Subgroup growth.''' In a series of works with Avinoam Mann and [[Dan Segal]], he characterised the finitely generated groups of polynomial [[subgroup growth]], combining tools from finite, algebraic and profinite groups and number theory.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lubotzky |first1=Alexander |last2=Mann |first2=Avinoam |last3=Segal |first3=Dan |title=Finitely generated groups of polynomial subgroup growth |journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=82 |year=1993 |pages=363–371 |doi=10.1007/BF02808118}}</ref> The subject is the theme of his monograph ''Subgroup Growth'' with Segal.
* '''Word metrics on lattices.''' With Shahar Mozes and [[M. S. Raghunathan]] he proved that for irreducible [[Lattice (discrete subgroup)|lattices]] in higher-rank semisimple Lie groups, the [[word metric]] is Lipschitz-equivalent to the metric induced from the ambient group, confirming a conjecture of Kazhdan.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lubotzky |first1=Alexander |last2=Mozes |first2=Shahar |last3=Raghunathan |first3=M. S. |title=The word and Riemannian metrics on lattices of semisimple groups |journal=[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]] |volume=91 |year=2000 |pages=5–53 |doi=10.1007/BF02698740}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==
=== Academy memberships and honorary degrees ===
* 2003: Listed by the [[Institute for Scientific Information]] as one of the world's most highly cited researchers in mathematics.<ref name="hayadan" />
* 2005: Elected a Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="amacad" /><ref>{{cite journal |title=American Academy Elections |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=52 |issue=7 |year=2005 |page=764 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200507/people.pdf}}</ref>
* 2006: [[Honorary degree|Honorary doctorate]] from the [[University of Chicago]] for his contributions to modern mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary Degrees |url=https://convocation.uchicago.edu/page/2000 |publisher=[[University of Chicago]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808032536/https://convocation.uchicago.edu/page/2000 |archive-date=8 August 2017 |url-status=dead |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2014: Elected to the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities add five new researchers to its prestigious ranks |url=https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Health/Israel-Academy-of-Sciences-and-Humanities-add-five-new-researchers-to-its-prestigious-ranks-385411 |work=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |year=2014 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2022: Elected an honorary member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="cv" /><ref>{{cite news |title=Új tagokat választott a Magyar Tudományos Akadémia |trans-title=The Hungarian Academy of Sciences has elected new members |url=https://infostart.hu/tudomany/2022/05/03/uj-tagokat-valasztott-a-magyar-tudomanyos-akademia |work=Infostart |language=hu |date=3 May 2022 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

=== European Research Council grants ===
Lubotzky has received the [[European Research Council]] (ERC) Advanced Grant three times, a distinction shared by very few researchers:
* 2008, for the project "Expander graphs in pure and applied mathematics";<ref>{{cite web |title=ERC Advanced Grant 2008 – list of principal investigators |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc_2008_adg_results_all%20domains.pdf |publisher=[[European Research Council]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2015, for "High-dimensional expanders";<ref>{{cite web |title=ERC Advanced Grants 2015 – list of principal investigators |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc_2015_adg_results_all_domains.pdf |publisher=European Research Council |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2020 (2019 call), for "Stability and testability: groups and codes".<ref>{{cite web |title=ERC Advanced Grants 2019 – list of principal investigators |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc-2019-adg-results-all-domains.pdf |publisher=European Research Council |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=פרופ' ישראלי קיבל בפעם ה-3 מענק יוקרתי |trans-title=Israeli professor receives prestigious grant for the third time |url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5709734,00.html |work=[[Ynet]] |language=he |date=6 April 2020 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

=== Honorary and plenary lectures ===
* 1994: Invited speaker in the algebra section of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM), Zürich.<ref name="jmm2011" />
* 1997 and 2016: Plenary speaker at the [[British Mathematical Colloquium]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BMC 1997 |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/BMC/1997/ |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=BMC 2016 |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/BMC/2016/ |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2011: [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] Colloquium Lectures at the [[Joint Mathematics Meetings]] in New Orleans, the first Israeli to be so honoured.<ref name="jmm2011" /><ref>{{cite news |title=Top Israeli Mathematician to Be Honored |url=https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/140788 |work=[[Arutz Sheva]] |date=23 November 2010 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2011: Mordell Lecture, [[University of Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mordell Lecturers |url=https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/mordell-lecturers |publisher=Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics, [[University of Cambridge]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2012: Simons Lectures, [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]];<ref>{{cite web |title=Simons Lecture Series – 2012 Lectures |url=https://math.mit.edu/news/seminars/simons12.php |publisher=MIT Department of Mathematics |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref> Takagi Lectures of the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]], Tokyo.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Lubotzky |first=Alexander |title=Ramanujan complexes and high dimensional expanders |journal=Japanese Journal of Mathematics |volume=9 |year=2014 |pages=137–169 |doi=10.1007/s11537-014-1265-z}}</ref>
* 2018: Plenary lecture, "High dimensional expanders", at the ICM in [[Rio de Janeiro]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Lubotzky: How computer science and math intertwine |url=https://impa.br/notices/matematica-e-ciencia-da-computacao-cada-vez-mais-interligadas/ |publisher=[[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|IMPA]] |date=7 August 2018 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Lubotzky |first=Alexander |chapter=High dimensional expanders |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM 2018) |volume=1 |pages=705–730 |publisher=World Scientific |year=2018}}</ref>

=== Prizes ===
* 1979: Landau Prize of [[Mifal HaPais]].<ref name="cv" />
* 1980–81: Bergman Memorial Prize of the [[United States – Israel Binational Science Foundation]].<ref name="cv" />
* 1991: [[Erdős Prize]] of the Israel Mathematical Union.<ref name="weizmann" /><ref name="cv" />
* 1993: [[Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize]] for the monograph ''Discrete Groups, Expanding Graphs and Invariant Measures''.<ref name="ffsb">{{cite web |title=El Premi – Guardonats |trans-title=The Prize – Laureates |url=https://ffsb.iec.cat/el-premi/ |publisher=Fundació Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer, [[Institut d'Estudis Catalans]] |language=ca |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2002: [[Yad Hanadiv|Rothschild Prize]] in mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Rothschild Prize – Recipients |url=https://www.yadhanadiv.org.il/the-rothschild-prize/ |publisher=[[Yad Hanadiv]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2002: Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize (second time) for the monograph ''Subgroup Growth'', with Dan Segal.<ref name="ffsb" /><ref>{{cite journal |title=Sunyer i Balaguer Prize Awarded |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=49 |issue=6 |year=2002 |page=687 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200206/people.pdf}}</ref>
* 2007: Rector's Prize of the Hebrew University for excellence in research and teaching.<ref>{{cite web |title=Einstein Institute of Mathematics – News |url=http://www.ma.huji.ac.il/info/prize.html |publisher=Hebrew University of Jerusalem |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525002639/http://www.ma.huji.ac.il/info/prize.html |archive-date=25 May 2011 |url-status=dead |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2018: [[Israel Prize]] in mathematics and computer science.<ref name="toi" /><ref>{{cite web |title=פרופ' אלכס לובוצקי |trans-title=Prof. Alex Lubotzky |url=https://www.gov.il/he/pages/alex-lubotzky |website=Israel Prize |publisher=[[Ministry of Education (Israel)|Israel Ministry of Education]] |language=he |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2022: Best Paper Award at the [[Symposium on Theory of Computing|ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing]] (STOC 2022), for the construction of good locally testable codes.<ref>{{cite web |title=STOC Best Paper Award |url=https://www.sigact.org/prizes/best_paper.html |publisher=[[ACM SIGACT]] |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2023: Frontiers of Science Award of the International Congress of Basic Science (ICBS), Beijing, for the same paper.<ref>{{cite web |title=Frontiers of Science Award |url=https://2023.icbs.cn/18009_1581229.html |publisher=International Congress of Basic Science |year=2023 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2024: [[IEEE Information Theory Society]] Paper Award, for the same paper.<ref>{{cite web |title=Information Theory Society Paper Award |url=https://www.itsoc.org/honors/information-theory-paper-award |publisher=IEEE Information Theory Society |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2025: Best Paper Award at the [[Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science|IEEE Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science]] (FOCS 2025), for the explicit construction of lossless vertex expanders.<ref name="focs25" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Congratulations to Prof. Alex Lubotzky and Assaf Reiner on winning the FOCS Best Paper Award |url=https://mathematics.huji.ac.il/news/congratulations-%C2%A0prof%C2%A0alex-lubotzky-assaf-reiner-winning-best-paper-award-focs-2025 |publisher=Einstein Institute of Mathematics, Hebrew University of Jerusalem |date=15 September 2025 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 1980 Lubotzky married Yardenna Roston, daughter of the literary scholar [[Murray Roston]]; she is a lecturer in art history and English and the author of a Hebrew book on artistic and traditional interpretation of the weekly Torah portion.<ref name="nonmathcv" /><ref>{{cite web |title=בין קודש למכחול: פרשנות אמנותית ופרשנות מסורתית לפרשת השבוע – חומש בראשית |trans-title=Brushes with the Bible: artistic and traditional interpretation of the weekly portion – Genesis |url=https://korenpub.co.il/products/brushes-with-the-biblehardcover-hebrew |publisher=[[Koren Publishers Jerusalem]] |language=he |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref> The couple have six children and many grandchildren.<ref name="weizmann" /> Their eldest son, [[Asael Lubotzky]], author of ''[[From the Wilderness and Lebanon]]'' and ''Not My Last Journey'', was severely wounded in the [[Battle of Bint Jbeil (2006)|Battle of Bint Jbeil]] during the [[2006 Lebanon War]] while serving as a platoon commander in the [[Golani Brigade]]; after a long rehabilitation he became a physician.<ref name="hayadan" /><ref>{{cite book |last=Lubotzky |first=Asael |author-link=Asael Lubotzky |title=[[From the Wilderness and Lebanon]] |year=2016 |publisher=[[Koren Publishers Jerusalem]] |isbn=978-1592644179}}</ref>

The Lubotzky family were among the founding residents of [[Efrat]], where they live.<ref name="nonmathcv" /><ref name="toi" />
